newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Aerolineas-American Air deal seen near.
newsitem.headline: Aerolineas-American Air deal seen near.

text.p: Argentina's Economy Minister Roque Fernandez on Friday said a deal between AMR Corp's American Airlines and Aerolineas Argentinas may be close at hand.
Fernandez told reporters that he had asked for a meeting in Washington with U.S. Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater to discuss the matter. The minister starts a visit to the United States Friday.

"Since the decision-making time is getting closer, we think a meeting is necessary to talk openly, above all about how they view the operation and what expectations there are of Argentina's role in the issue," Ferandez told reporters.

Earlier this year, the main shareholders in Aerolineas asked American and Continental Airlines Inc to make bids for a stake of about 20 percent in the Latin American airline, which is operated by Spain's state-owned air carrier Iberia.
A 63.35 percent stake in Aerolineas is controlled by a group formed by Spanish state holding company SEPI, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc and Bankers Trust New York Corp.
Iberia, or Iberia Lineas Aereas de Espana SA, directly owns 20 percent of Aerolineas, and Argentina's government has a five percent in the airline.
Fernandez said the meeting with Slater was aimed at finding out about how U.S. regulations would affect a possible link between Aerolineas and American Airlines.
